questions.title: BufferedReader Role
questions.description: Java offers several I/O classes for reading text files. Which class wraps around a FileReader to add internal buffering and provides the readLine() method that returns one full line at a time?
questions.Option1: BufferedWriter
questions.Option2: BufferedReader
questions.Option3: ObjectInputStream
questions.Option4: StringReader

questions.title: FileWriter Append Flag
questions.description: A program opens an existing file and writes to it. The file data.txt already contains exactly the text 'old data'. Study the snippet and decide what data.txt contains after it runs.
questions.Option1: old dataentry one (the new text is appended after the old text)
questions.Option2: entry one (the old content is erased)
questions.Option3: old data (the new text is discarded)
questions.Option4: entry oneold data (new text is written before the old text)

questions.title: readLine At End Of File
questions.description: A student loops over a text file with BufferedReader as shown. What makes this loop terminate correctly when the file runs out of lines?
questions.Option1: readLine() returns an empty string at end of file
questions.Option2: readLine() throws IOException at end of file
questions.Option3: readLine() returns null at end of file, so the loop condition fails
questions.Option4: readLine() returns the word EOF at end of file

questions.title: Checked IOException Rule
questions.description: java.io.IOException is a checked exception. What does the Java compiler require from code that calls file methods which can throw it?
questions.Option1: The call must sit in a try block with a matching catch, or the enclosing method must declare it with throws
questions.Option2: Nothing special, because IOException is unchecked
questions.Option3: The class must extend IOException to handle it
questions.Option4: The call is allowed only inside constructors

questions.title: Serializable Marker Interface
questions.description: java.io.Serializable is usually called a marker interface. What does that mean?
questions.Option1: It is an abstract class with one abstract method to override
questions.Option2: It declares no methods; it only marks a class as eligible for object serialization
questions.Option3: It provides a default writeObject implementation
questions.Option4: It automatically encrypts every field of the class

questions.title: PrintWriter Close Discipline
questions.description: A PrintWriter collects characters in an internal buffer before they reach the disk. A program writes ten lines with println but exits without calling close() or flush(). What is the most likely result?
questions.Option1: The JVM crashes with an IOException on exit
questions.Option2: The file grows to twice its expected size
questions.Option3: Java flushes the buffer automatically after every println, so the file is complete
questions.Option4: Some or all buffered lines may never reach the file, leaving it empty or incomplete

questions.title: File delete Return Value
questions.description: The File class models a file path and offers file operations. What does f.delete() return when called on a File object?
questions.Option1: A boolean that is true when the file was successfully deleted
questions.Option2: Nothing; it throws an exception when deletion fails
questions.Option3: The name of the deleted file as a String
questions.Option4: An int with the number of bytes freed

questions.title: Truncating Write Constructor
questions.description: A program must replace the entire content of data.txt with new text. Which constructor opens the file for writing and discards any previous content?
questions.Option1: new FileWriter("data.txt", true)
questions.Option2: new FileWriter("data.txt")
questions.Option3: new FileReader("data.txt")
questions.Option4: new File("data.txt")

questions.title: ObjectInputStream Read Type
questions.description: After saving an object with ObjectOutputStream.writeObject, a program reads it back with ObjectInputStream.readObject. What does readObject return, and what must the calling code do?
questions.Option1: It returns the exact original class, so no cast is needed
questions.Option2: It returns a String description of the object
questions.Option3: It returns Object, so the code must cast it back to the original class
questions.Option4: It returns void and fills a field of the stream

questions.title: Which Fields Are Skipped
questions.description: A class implements java.io.Serializable and one of its objects is written with ObjectOutputStream. Which kind of field is NOT stored in the file?
questions.Option1: An array of Serializable objects
questions.Option2: A private String field
questions.Option3: A final int field
questions.Option4: A field marked transient

questions.title: serialVersionUID Purpose
questions.description: Every Serializable class can declare a private static final long serialVersionUID. What role does this number play when an object is deserialized?
questions.Option1: It decides how many objects one stream may hold
questions.Option2: It stamps the class version; when the stored value differs from the class value, deserialization throws InvalidClassException
questions.Option3: It encrypts the serialized bytes for security
questions.Option4: It chooses the default file name for ObjectOutputStream

questions.title: Transient And Static Round Trip
questions.description: The class in the snippet is serialized and later deserialized. The saved object had name 'app' and secret 'xyz'. Just before deserializing, the program sets Config.mode = 'night'. What are the field values of the deserialized object? Recall that transient instance fields and static fields are never written by the serialization engine.
questions.Option1: name is app, secret is null, mode is night
questions.Option2: name is app, secret is xyz, mode is day
questions.Option3: name is app, secret is null, mode is day
questions.Option4: name is app, secret is xyz, mode is night

questions.title: Catch Superclass Catches Subclass
questions.description: The file missing.txt does not exist, and the FileReader constructor throws FileNotFoundException when it cannot open a file. FileNotFoundException is a subclass of IOException. What does the program print?
questions.Option1: opened
questions.Option2: IO problem
questions.Option3: The program crashes with an uncaught FileNotFoundException
questions.Option4: It does not compile because FileNotFoundException must be caught before IOException

questions.title: println Versus write
questions.description: Predict the exact content of out.txt after the snippet runs. println writes its text followed by a line separator, while write writes characters only.
questions.Option1: Two lines: sun, then moon
questions.Option2: A single line sunmoon with no line separator at the end
questions.Option3: A single line containing sunmoon followed by a line separator
questions.Option4: Only moon, because write is replaced by println

questions.title: writeObject Requirement
questions.description: A developer runs the snippet with a plain class Student that has a String field and an int field, and implements no interfaces. What happens?
questions.Option1: Compilation fails because writeObject accepts only Serializable references
questions.Option2: The object is written, but only primitive fields are stored
questions.Option3: A FileNotFoundException is thrown because stu.dat does not exist
questions.Option4: NotSerializableException is thrown at runtime because Student does not implement Serializable

questions.title: FileReader Versus FileInputStream
questions.description: Which statement correctly distinguishes FileReader from FileInputStream?
questions.Option1: FileReader reads characters using a character encoding, while FileInputStream reads raw bytes
questions.Option2: FileReader is always buffered, while FileInputStream is never buffered
questions.Option3: FileInputStream reads text lines, while FileReader reads binary objects
questions.Option4: Both are abstract classes that cannot be instantiated directly

questions.title: Version Mismatch On Load
questions.description: A License object was serialized to disk last month, when the class declared serialVersionUID = 1L. The class was later edited and now declares serialVersionUID = 2L, as shown. A program now reads the old file with ObjectInputStream.readObject. What happens?
questions.Option1: It succeeds and the key field is restored; versions are ignored
questions.Option2: Deserialization fails with an InvalidClassException because the stored version 1L differs from the class version 2L
questions.Option3: It fails with NotSerializableException
questions.Option4: It succeeds but the key field comes back null

questions.title: Object Stream Order
questions.description: Two objects are written into one object stream and then read back as shown. What are the values of a and b after the two reads?
questions.Option1: a is 42 and b is first, in reverse write order
questions.Option2: a is first and b is null because only one object fits per stream
questions.Option3: The second readObject call throws EOFException
questions.Option4: a is the String first and b is the Integer 42, in the same order they were written

questions.title: Append Then Truncate Log
questions.description: A logging utility runs the two writes shown, in the same program, one after another. What does log.txt contain after the program finishes? Recall that PrintWriter(String) recreates the file from scratch while FileWriter(file, true) opens the file in append mode.
questions.Option1: Two lines: one, then two
questions.Option2: A single line: one
questions.Option3: A single line: two, because the second PrintWriter recreated the file from scratch
questions.Option4: A single line: onetwo

questions.title: Deserialization Skips Constructor
questions.description: A Serializable class Point has a constructor that sets its field tag to 'fresh'. An object whose tag is 'stored' was serialized earlier. Which statement is TRUE when that object is loaded back with readObject?
questions.Option1: The constructor runs again, so tag becomes fresh
questions.Option2: The constructor is NOT invoked; the tag field is restored from the stream as stored
questions.Option3: The constructor runs only when serialVersionUID is declared
questions.Option4: Deserialization fails because every class needs its constructor
